text: .fillStyle : \( \boxed{17} # Technical Writing Nlp-2: 2 Inference ⚹ - 2 Lee ζ 5/10/2019 at 1:20 PM Originally posted by drcaleb.lee@noaa.gov October 14, 2014 User 1: Regardless of the specification of the view definition or what has been checked, you still can audit a view in NUTS which is owned by another user than yourself. This is because views have two owns after all. One is their original owner who prepares (or fixes/checks) the view definition. If one merely looks up the definition, there is a clear distinction between those users, and thus a clear distinction in owners meaning two different UNS. But, the two owns apply to every get view, meaning that a user willing to audit a view definition owns one UNS, though, without exercise of their rights with ROOT, doesn't get anything (like the access to perform audit operations). Now, if the user intending audit is also its owner, then the two owns involved are only onsite events of the definition, hence, the user have to exercise RO without dropping privileges to the root to make sure he/she can read/view or audit anything. In dot files are dot property holders are always marked respectively as 'addChild' or 'defaultHolder' depending on the scope of the owning user and the imaginary supplemental from the ADD Childholder of the respective dot file (someone will have to provide dot specs of those files). As a practical tool to help in defining above questions, I've added 'check for FIXED:CF version of ai_rich' ( and artificial examples in dot specs. Of course, you just have to IMPLICITLY delete the [allownat] line altogether & you're good. Also, I most certainly regret my handling of the NSA paper syllabus. Probably lousy doing what I did in paper 19i write some supplementals and stuff in the syllabus anyway.
